content:
morgan: heads-up — during the eu-west-1 evening deploy we saw ~120 inference pods fall back to cpu-only nodes for ~6m before eviction. some customers saw degraded latency.
morgan: early hypothesis: autoscaler scale-down + tolerationSeconds race. pods tolerate a GPU taint briefly and get scheduled on leftover cpu nodes when a GPU node is drained.
devin: do you have the pod spec / toleration snippet? could be a taint key mismatch too (we had that once when copying from an old chart).
morgan: snippet from the helm release (sanitized):
```yaml
tolerations:
  - key: "redwood.io/gpu"
    operator: "Equal"
    value: "present"
    effect: "NoSchedule"
    tolerationSeconds: 300
nodeSelector:
  workload: "inference"
```
morgan: but nodes are tainted with `redwood.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule` (note the `.com` vs `.io`). so toleration didn't match; cluster-autoscaler then removed idle gpu node and scheduler placed pods on cpu nodes that temporarily reported GPU resources (weird), then kubelet eviction later.
ash: ouch. that key flip would totally bypass the isolation. how did the nodes end up with `.com`? rollout script?
sana: I think the GPU node bootstrap uses the gpu-launch-template user-data which sets taints from cloud-init, that template was updated in the launch config PR last week (owner: infra-launch).
liam: cost impact: if pods ran on cpu nodes they consumed non-GPU vCPU units and increased p95 latency — also some requests retried which spiked API usage. estimate ~1.2k USD for the 40m incident window on eu-west-1.
ops-bot: @morgan created incident INC-2026-0422 and runbook attached: https://internal/incidents/INC-2026-0422
devin: immediate mitigation options:
- patch tolerations in the live helm release to match `.com` key (fast)
- or patch node taints to `.io` (dangerous if other clusters expect `.com`)
- cordon cpu-only nodes and drain to force reschedule to true GPU nodes (if available)
- set `tolerationSeconds: null` so pods never temporarily tolerate short-lived taints
morgan: I'm leaning patch -> helm rollback + follow-up to standardize key. but also want autoscaler flags tuned to avoid the drain+scale-down race. suggestions?
devin: cluster-autoscaler flags that help: `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` (if using local cache), adjust `--scale-down-delay-after-add` and `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to give pods buffer. Also `--expendable-pods-priority-cutoff` if using priorities.
ash: longer term we should prefer nodeAffinity over relying solely on tolerations for GPU workloads: `requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` with nodeSelectorTerms ensures pods won't land on non-gpu nodes even if taint matching is wrong.
sana: agree. sample affinity: 
```yaml
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
        - key: "redwood.com/gpu"
          operator: In
          values: ["true"]
```
This plus taints is defense in depth.
liam: can we add a validating webhook to fail deploys when toleration or affinity keys don't match the canonical `redwood.com/gpu` value? that'll prevent future flips.
morgan: good idea. ownership: infra-launch will revert the launch-template taint key to `redwood.com/gpu` and open a PR to standardize across init scripts. I'll patch the service helm chart tolerations to accept both keys for a transitional window.
morgan: action items:
- infra-launch: revert template and tag images used in bootstrap (owner: @sana)
- infra-helm: patch toleration key to support `.com` and `.io` (owner: @morgan)
- autoscaler: change scale-down-unneeded-time to 10m in eu-west for gpu nodepools (owner: @devin)
- platform: plan validating webhook for taint/affinity enforcement (owner: @ash)
- ops: cordon & drain the affected cpu-only nodes (temporary) (owner: @ops-bot)
devin: small follow-up: if you keep tolerationSeconds > 0 we risk short windows where pods can land on wrong nodes during transient taint toggles. prefer using non-temporary tolerations for GPU-only pods or required nodeAffinity.
ash: also add a PodDisruptionBudget small PSB to protect running long-lived inference replicas during node operations.
liam: for reporting, can we run a query to find pods that requested nvidia.com/gpu but were scheduled onto nodes without the label? quick kql/metrics would help quantify surface area.
morgan: I'll run `kubectl get pods -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Running` with custom jq to spot mismatches and post results in the incident doc.
k8s-bot: reminder: helm release `inference-svc` in eu-west-1 v2.4.1 -> pending patch. use `helm upgrade --reuse-values` for hotfix.
ops-bot: cordon/drain done for node euw2-cpu-12, euw2-cpu-19. pods rebalanced to gpu nodes, p95 recovered.
morgan: thanks everyone. I'll open the two PRs and share links here. tagging follow-ups for next infra retro. :thumbsup:
